articles.headline: Nashville turf temps of 157 F melt cleats, send Sirianni for IV
articles.description: Players cleats were melting and head coach Nick Sirianni needed an IV as a result of extreme heat conditions at Nissan Stadium during Sunday's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, a 24-20 Eagles win.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Players cleats were melting and head coach Nick Sirianni needed an IV as a result of extreme heat conditions at Nissan Stadium during Sunday's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, a 24-20 Eagles win.

The temperature on the turf reached 157 degrees Fahrenheit per the television broadcast.

Left tackle Jordan Mailata, the team's NFLPA player rep in 2025, said this is another reason why the union should push for the league to do away with turf surfaces.

"I've never thought about how hot a stadium can be if it's turf. [The heat] just sits there and bounces up into you," he said. "We've got to bring it up. This is why we want all grass fields, to create a standard of play in the league where we're not putting players in dangerous positions if we don't have to."

Center Cam Jurgens noted postgame that his feet were "burning, still hurting." Jurgens said he went through multiple pairs of cleats due them melting.

"Halftime was like a NASCAR pit crew helping me get ready for the second half," he said. "That turf was just radiating."

The temperature in Nashville for Sunday's 12 p.m. (CT) kickoff was 95 degrees with a heat index of around 105. A "heat dome" had settled over the area in recent weeks, with high pressure in the atmosphere pushing heat towards the surface and trapping it there.

Titans safety Amani Hooker said the midsoles of his cleats "melted completely off" in the season opener against New York Jets. Mailata said he rolled his ankles twice in the game and wondered it could be the result of his shoes bending because the plastic in the bottom of his cleats got soft.

Television cameras showed a member of the Titans having his cleats sprayed with water to cool them off.

"It was hot as s---," Sirianni said. "I didn't play a snap and I had to get an IV. I so appreciate how much the guys prepared, I so appreciate how much they fought through because it wasn't easy."

There was some conversation after the game centered around the idea that teams would not be permitted to practice outdoors in such conditions, making it curious why the league continues to schedule early afternoon September games in hot weather climates.

The Eagles played in similar conditions each of the past two seasons in Tampa Bay. Safety Reed Blankenship had to leave the Bucs game in 2024 with a heat-related illness that was considered pretty serious at the time.

The Eagles left for Nashville on Friday, a day earlier than normal, to try and acclimate to the weather. They held a walkthrough in the middle of the day Saturday to try and get players used to the conditions.

"It was one of the top five toughest games I've been a part of," said tackle Lane Johnson, a 14-year veteran. "It was a mental test for everyone involved."

articles.headline: Colts rule out Alec Pierce with left heel injury vs. Chiefs
articles.description: Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce was ruled out of Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs after suffering a left heel injury with 1:45 left in the first quarter.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce was ruled out of Sunday night's game against the Kansas City Chiefs after suffering a left heel injury with 1:45 left in the first quarter.

The injury is to the same leg on which Pierce had surgery in March.

Pierce, the Colts' top wideout, was unable to put any weight on his left leg and needed assistance to the injury tent at Arrowhead Stadium. After an initial exam in the tent, Pierce was carted to the locker room and, according to the NBC broadcast, was taken to the X-ray room at the stadium.

Pierce was initially listed as questionable to return before quickly being downgraded to out in the second quarter.

Pierce, who signed a four-year $114 million contract in March, was expected to be a centerpiece of the Colts' offense this season after undergoing ankle surgery in March to address a lingering condition.

But his recovery from the procedure spilled into training camp and lingered past the preseason. He finally returned to practice late last month and was expecting to ramp up his playing time in the weeks to come after being cleared to play in Week 1.

With Pierce out, veteran receiver Laquon Treadwell was taking a majority of his snaps against the Chiefs.

articles.headline: Brock Purdy keeps 49ers rolling with 'MVP' game vs. Dolphins
articles.description: Brock Purdy authored a near-perfect game at quarterback in the 49ers' 35-13 win over the rebuilding Dolphins, ending the the day with a 99.7 QBR.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- As San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy wrapped up his media availability after Sunday's win against the Miami Dolphins, linebacker Fred Warner greeted Purdy, pointed to him and declared "MVP."

Just two weeks into the season, it's far too early for any sweeping award declarations but Purdy's performance against the rebuilding Dolphins on Sunday was so close to perfect that Warner wanted the world to know he sees where Purdy could go in his fifth NFL season.

"Brock is unbelievable," Warner said. "I've spoken on how great of a preseason he had and his camp, his command of the offense, but it's different. We get judged on those three hours that we're out there. For him to be operating the offense the way he is right now, it doesn't matter who the other pieces are. As long as Brock's the one that's being the point guard, I know we're good."

After a week-long stay in Melbourne, Australia to open the season, there were plenty of questions this week about whether the Niners might have a letdown against a Dolphins team that is in the first year of a roster teardown.

Purdy heard that chatter and silenced it with one of his best and most complete games as the Niners rolled to a 35-13 win to improve to 2-0. Combined with their 27-7 win against the Los Angeles Rams last week, San Francisco has started the season with back-to-back 20-plus point wins to open a season for the first time in franchise history.

With Purdy at the controls, the Niners scored a touchdown on each of their first five offensive possessions, the first time they've done that in the past 45 seasons, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

After receiver Deebo Samuel dropped Purdy's third pass attempt, Purdy rattled off 18 straight completions, a streak that only ended when officials flagged him for intentional grounding on his final pass of the day.

Purdy said he wasn't even aware of the streak as he was too busy trying to help push the Niners to a bigger lead after getting just two offensive possessions in the first half.

"I honestly didn't know until towards the end, fourth quarter maybe," Purdy said. "For me, every play, every drive mattered. It wasn't like we went out there and just blew these guys out. It was a game. And that's what we're saying. That's the NFL. That's where my head space was at."

By the time it was over, Purdy was 20-of-22 for 287 yards with two touchdowns for a 99.7 QBR and tacked on 30 rushing yards with another score. In the process, he became the second player in NFL history with 250-plus passing yards with a completion rate of 90% or better in multiple games, joining Derek Carr at that mark.

Purdy also is the first quarterback in league history to hit both those marks in a game with 30 or more rushing yards. Entering the Sunday night game, Purdy leads the league in QBR (95.9) and completion percentage (80.4%) and is tied for fifth in touchdown passes (five).

articles.headline: Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now
articles.description: This is Man United's worst start in a Premier League season in 12 years. Is there any reason to believe a turnaround is ahead?
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック、マンUのポジティブな面を見出そうとするも現在は好材料が乏しい状況
articles.descriptionJa: これはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドにとって過去12年間で最悪のプレミアリーグ開幕スタートとなった。巻き返しを信じられる理由は何かあるのだろうか？
articles.body:
LONDON -- For Michael Carrick, the international break won't feel like much of a break at all.

The games will stop, but after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Fulham on Sunday, the spotlight and the scrutiny will remain. It's going to be a long three weeks for United's coach.

It could have been even worse. Matheus Cunha's 89th-minute equalizer prevented a first defeat at Craven Cottage in 17 years and stopped the pressure on Carrick ramping up to another level.

After back-to-back home defeats to Manchester City and Brighton, three consecutive losses would have left United's decision-makers with some thinking to do while the players jet off to join their national teams.

As it is, a point at Fulham will at least stop the bleeding -- there's not much to shout about. Five points from five games is United's worst start to a Premier League season for more than a decade. And that's after a run of fixtures that appeared on paper to be relatively manageable.

"It's not been ideal," Carrick admitted. "I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But at the same time, I'm not despondent and down because I think we're showing some good signs as well.

"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points from it."

Though Carrick was keen to find the positives, the most damning part of the day was perhaps the assessment of his former United teammate Gary Neville. The pair played together at Old Trafford for four years, but when Fulham went ahead midway through the second half, Neville did not hold back.

"I've watched Manchester United since the age of 5," he said. "That's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen them play."

Given some of the disastrous displays over the past decade, it was quite a statement. Neville's outburst -- during which he branded parts of the performance as "pathetic" -- was prompted by a calamitous Fulham goal.

Kobbie Mainoo's pass into midfield was telegraphed by Calvin Bassey, who was too strong for Cunha. Then the Fulham defender was allowed to advance unchallenged into the penalty area before firing a tame shot at Senne Lammens.

But when things aren't going well, even the most innocuous situations can turn into something else. This time, Bassey's shot hit Lammens before rebounding back toward the goal off Lisandro Martínez.

A scrambling Lammens chose to use his feet rather than his hands to stop the ball and succeeded only in booting it into the net. It was either bad luck or symptomatic of a United team struggling with the confidence to make decisive decisions.

Self-belief, or lack of it, is not the only issue for Carrick to address. There's a feeling among some fans that United have not looked fit enough during the early part of the season.

Running stats aren't everything, but at the end of the 90 minutes, Fulham's players had covered an extra 6 kilometers more than United's players. There were certainly times during the game when it appeared obvious that the home side was quicker, faster and sharper.

articles.headline: Eagles' Broadway jab at Titans leads NFL Week 2 trolls
articles.description: Teams across the NFL came with petty postgame energy after wins in Week 2, led by the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
With half of the league looking to remain undefeated heading into Week 2, a win could lead to an even sweeter troll. Case in point? The Philadelphia Eagles.

The Eagles used a late two-minute drive to steal a 24-20 win against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

Tennessee took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left and needed one stop for its first win of the season. But Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts led his team down the field with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a 3-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Darius Cooper with nine seconds left. It marked the Eagles' latest winning passing touchdown since 2012, according to ESPN Research.

Nashville is home to the famous Broadway Street, but Philadelphia has its own notable street too: "Broad Street." Therefore, the Eagles posted a graphic of an Eagle on a "Broadway" street sign but covered "way" with a sticky note that read: "Street," putting a spin on Nashville's area.

Here are more of the top trolls from NFL Week 2.

Carolina Panthers 34, Atlanta Falcons 3

Carolina defeated its NFC South foe on the road Sunday in convincing fashion.

Panthers quarterback Bryce Young passed for 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to tight end Darren Waller. Carolina forced five turnovers -- three interceptions and two fumbles -- as Atlanta had only 286 total yards of offense.

Carolina's blowout win came with an equally dominant social media performance. It first shared a victory post with the score and caption: "Feelin' Peachy," a reference to Georgia being known as the Peach State. The Panthers then posted a graphic of a Panther eating a bird's egg with the caption: "We cooked."

New Orleans Saints 24, Baltimore Ravens 17

The Saints faced a 17-9 deficit heading into the fourth quarter but responded with consecutive touchdowns -- the final one coming with 1:28 left. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw an interception on the ensuing drive, and New Orleans secured the victory.

The NFC South team directed its troll toward an unlikely source: a Baltimore fan who had choice words for Saints fans on X. They wrote that Saints fans were "talking crazier than Colts fans," the Ravens' Week 1 opponent, and they'd similarly learn the "hard way" like Indianapolis' followers. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis last Sunday.

New Orleans remembered the slight, quoting the post with a video of wide receiver Chris Olave celebrating his fourth-quarter touchdown with the caption: "Love those crazy Saints fans."

Minnesota Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3

Another divisional game brought another troll, this time from the Minnesota Vikings.

Minnesota kept Chicago in check after the Bears put up 59 points in a Week 1 victory. The Vikings forced two turnovers, including one as Chicago running back D'Andre Swift fumbled while diving for a touchdown. The Bears reached the red zone again but had a field goal attempt blocked with 6:23 left. Minnesota got one more stop to claim the win.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes
articles.description: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Sunday night drip

Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner might have had the best outfit ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Buckner wore a navy and black silk suit made by Gentleman's Playbook. It was a bold and unique choice.

Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce also showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes, rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multicolored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

Commanders' rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was among the best dressed players during the arrivals for the Sunday afternoon games. Styles arrived in a grey suit, with his initials embroidered on the collar in gold.

Here are more notable arrivals from the 4 p.m. slate:

Best of 1 p.m. arrivals

Cincinnati Bengals defensive lineman Myles Murphy was the best dressed during Sunday's early slate. Murphy arrived wearing a Gallery Department Logan canvas trucker vest with black cargo pants. His Bottega Veneta woven duffle bag was a strong complementary piece.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns. Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped and white shoes.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Here are some of the other memorable fits from Sunday's 1 p.m. slate:

Thursday night's best fit

To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

articles.headline: White Sox keep pace in the AL Central with a rain-soaked 8-1 win over the Tigers
articles.description: — Sam Antonacci had a two-run double in a three-run fourth inning and the Chicago White Sox kept pace in the AL Central and eliminated the Detroit Tigers from playoff contention with a rain-soaked 8-1 victory Sunday.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Sam Antonacci had a two-run double in a three-run fourth inning and the Chicago White Sox kept pace in the AL Central and eliminated the Detroit Tigers from playoff contention with a rain-soaked 8-1 victory Sunday.


              The White Sox remained a game behind the Cleveland Guardians in the division and hold a three-game lead over the Houston Astros and Toronto Blue Jays for the third wild card.


              The start was delayed 3 hours, 50 minutes by rain and most of the game was played in a swirling mist.


              Davis Martin threw 4 1/3 scoreless innings for the White Sox, striking out six, allowing three hits and walking three. He failed to record a win for his 15th straight appearance dating to June 10.


              Huascar Brazoban (6-2), activated from the injured list earlier Sunday, pitched a scoreless sixth for the victory.


              Trevor Richards pitched two innings for the 205th White Sox relief outing of 1 1/3 innings or more, a major league record.


              Braden Montgomery started the scoring with an RBI double in the second. Kyle Teel singled home Antonacci after his double in the fourth. Chase Meidroth hit his 15th home run in the fifth, a two-run shot into the left-field bullpen.


              Max Clark broke up the shutout with a sacrifice fly in the top of the eighth.


              Detroit reliever Brant Hurler walked in a run in the bottom of the inning and Randal Grichuk followed with a sacrifice fly to make it 8-1.


              Detroit starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed three runs on four hits and three walks in 3 2/3 innings before leaving with a trainer after Antonacci's double.


              Eduardo Valencia had three hits for the Tigers.


              Up next
              The Tigers have not announced a starter for Monday's opener of a three-game series against Washington. The White Sox are off Monday before before beginning a three-game series at Kansas City, with LHP Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.41 ERA) starting Tuesday against LHP Daniel Lynch IV (6-6, 3.29).
